newsitem.title: FRANCE: Millers want EU to restore flour subsidies -ONIC.
newsitem.headline: Millers want EU to restore flour subsidies -ONIC.

text.p: French flour millers, anxious to ensure a steady business flow until the new harvest, are pressing the European Union to restore subsidies on flour exports, French grain officials said.

Alain Moulinier, boss of cereals office ONIC, told a news conference that millers had asked French authorities to raise their concerns over disruption to flour exports when the European Union's grain panel meets on Thursday.
Milling firms say the disruption is caused by current wheat export taxes of seven Ecus a tonne.
"Millers are asking for export subsidies...They did not get much response from the Commission's services and they say they need the support of French authorities to get something," Moulinier said.
Moulinier, who also urged the EU to drop a controversial tax on wheat exports and start exporting grain as soon as possible, said a refund of zero Ecus for flour would be "a minimum".
"It would not be enough to export on world markets but it would be enough for nearby destinations," he said.
Moulinier also said that millers were more vulnerable than grain exporters to sudden disruptions in export flows because they had to keep flour mills running all year round.
On May 14, the European Union restored taxes on soft wheat grain and flour exports to keep domestic prices and supplies under control in the face of rising world prices.
But since then prices have eased and exporters have pressed the EU to restore subsidies, while the Commission has said it is right to be cautious until the next harvest is in.
